title: Work and career
focus: daitto, sidhanto, podonnoti, istefa, sakkhatkar, kormochari, protishthan, lokkho, onumoti, chhuti newa, porishrom, abhigyota, dokkhota
body:
# Work and career

Office life in Kolkata is half English: meeting, boss, deadline, salary. But the Bengali words for responsibility, decisions, experience and resignation come up constantly, and you need them to talk about work with parents, relatives and anyone outside the office.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| daitto | দায়িত্ব | responsibility |
| sidhanto | সিদ্ধান্ত | decision |
| podonnoti | পদোন্নতি | promotion |
| istefa | ইস্তফা | resignation |
| sakkhatkar | সাক্ষাৎকার | interview |
| kormochari | কর্মচারী | employee |
| sohokormi | সহকর্মী | colleague |
| protishthan | প্রতিষ্ঠান | organisation, institution |
| lokkho | লক্ষ্য | goal, aim |
| onumoti | অনুমতি | permission |
| porishrom | পরিশ্রম | hard work |
| abhigyota | অভিজ্ঞতা | experience |
| dokkhota | দক্ষতা | skill |
| joggota | যোগ্যতা | qualification |
| obosor | অবসর | retirement |

## Which word?

- **English or Bengali?** In the office people say *promotion*, *interview*, *resign kora*, *apply kora*, *training*, *colleague*. *podonnoti*, *sakkhatkar*, *istefa*, *abedon*, *proshikkhon* and *sohokormi* are what you read in the paper and hear on the news, and what an older relative might use. Know both.
- **maine vs beton vs salary**: *maine* is the warm, spoken Kolkata word for monthly pay. *beton* is formal and official. *salary* is what most office workers say.
- **sidhanto vs sidhanto newa**: the noun is *sidhanto*; you *take* a decision: *sidhanto newa*, never *kora*.
- **chakri jawa vs istefa dewa**: *istefa dewa* is quitting on your own. *chakri jawa* (literally "the job goes") is losing it.

## Examples

- **ei kaj-ta ami samle nebo**: I'll handle this
- **ei project-er puro daitto amar**: The whole responsibility for this project is mine
- **ekhono kono sidhanto nini**: I haven't made a decision yet
- **o gelo mashe istefa diyechhe**: She resigned last month
- **eto bochhor porishrom korar por or podonnoti holo**: After years of hard work he got promoted
- **ei kaj-er jonno tin bochhor-er abhigyota lagbe**: This job needs three years' experience
- **office-e ajkal khub kajer chap**: There's a lot of work pressure at the office these days
- **corona-r somoy onek-er chakri chole gechhilo**: Many people lost their jobs during Covid
- **baba gelo bochhor obosor niyechhen**: Dad retired last year

cards.Example: ei project-er puro daitto amar: The whole responsibility for this project is mine
cards.Notes: daitto newa = take responsibility; daitto-shil = responsible (person).

cards.Example: eta khub kothin sidhanto chhilo: It was a very hard decision
cards.Notes: The collocation is sidhanto newa (to take a decision), not sidhanto kora.

cards.Example: ekhono kono sidhanto nini: I haven't made a decision yet
cards.Notes: Fully conversational. 'decide kora' is also heard.

cards.Example: eto bochhor porishrom korar por or podonnoti holo: After years of hard work he got promoted
cards.Notes: Formal/news word. In speech almost everyone says 'promotion pawa'.

cards.Example: o gelo mashe istefa diyechhe: She resigned last month
cards.Notes: istefa dewa. Also common: 'resign kora'.

cards.Example: kal ekta sakkhatkar achhe: I have an interview tomorrow
cards.Notes: Formal and news register; in speech 'interview' is far more common.

cards.Example: ei company-te panchsho kormochari achhe: This company has five hundred employees
cards.Notes: sorkari kormochari = government employee. 'staff' is also used.

cards.Example: uni ekta boro protishthan-e kaj koren: She works at a big organisation
cards.Notes: Covers companies, schools, NGOs. Casual speech often just says 'company'.

cards.Example: amar lokkho holo panch bochhor-e nijer byabsa khola: My goal is to start my own business in five years
cards.Notes: Also 'target' and 'to notice': lokkho kora. Not lokkhon (symptom).

cards.Example: boss-er onumoti chhara eta kora jabe na: We can't do this without the boss's permission
cards.Notes: onumoti newa / dewa. Formal-ish but common.

cards.English: to take time off (leave from work)
cards.Example: ami kal chhuti nichhi: I'm taking tomorrow off
cards.Notes: 'leave' is common in offices: leave newa. chhuti alone = holiday/day off.

cards.Example: porishrom korle fol pabe: If you work hard you'll see results
cards.Notes: porishrom kora = to work hard; porishromi = hardworking. khatuni is the more casual 'toil'.

cards.Example: ei kaj-er jonno tin bochhor-er abhigyota lagbe: This job needs three years' experience
cards.Notes: Also an experience you had: bhalo abhigyota holo = it was a good experience.

cards.Example: computer-e or dokkhota khub bhalo: He's very skilled with computers
cards.Notes: dokkho = skilled, efficient. 'skill' is used in office talk.

cards.Example: amar ek sohokormi kal chhere dichhe: A colleague of mine is leaving tomorrow
cards.Notes: Formal-ish; in speech 'colleague' or 'office-er lok' is common.

cards.Example: o chhoy mash dhore bekar bose achhe: He's been sitting at home unemployed for six months
cards.Notes: bekar bose thaka is the usual phrase. Can also mean 'useless'.

cards.Example: rajye bekarotto barchhe: Unemployment in the state is rising
cards.Notes: News word; bekar is the adjective for a person.

cards.English: to apply (for a job, a loan)
cards.Example: ami tin-te chakri-te abedon korechhi: I've applied for three jobs
cards.Notes: In speech 'apply kora' is very common; abedon is the written form/application.

cards.Example: ei pod-er jonno or joggota nei: He doesn't have the qualifications for this post
cards.Notes: joggo = deserving, eligible. Also 'worth': or joggota achhe = she deserves it.

cards.Example: office-e ajkal khub kajer chap: There's a lot of work pressure at the office these days
cards.Notes: chap = pressure. 'pressure' and 'tension' are also used in English.

cards.English: to lose one's job (be fired, laid off)
cards.Example: corona-r somoy onek-er chakri chole gechhilo: Many people lost their jobs during Covid
cards.Notes: The job is the subject: or chakri gechhe. Office English: 'fire kora'.

cards.Example: baba gelo bochhor obosor niyechhen: Dad retired last year
cards.Notes: obosor newa = to retire. Also 'free time': obosor somoy. 'retire kora' also common.

cards.Example: notun kormochari-der ek mash proshikkhon hoy: New employees get a month of training
cards.Notes: Formal. In speech 'training' is normal.

cards.English: to handle / manage (a situation, a task)
cards.Example: ei kaj-ta ami samle nebo: I'll handle this
cards.Notes: Also handling people or a crisis: poristhiti samlano.

cards.Example: ei mash-e maine ekhono dhoke ni: This month's salary hasn't come in yet
cards.Notes: Spoken Kolkata word. beton is formal; office workers often say 'salary'.

cards.Example: sign korar age chukti-ta bhalo kore porho: Read the contract carefully before signing
cards.Notes: Also treaties between countries. 'contract' is common in business talk.

cards.Example: tomar sapholyo-r jonno obhinondon: Congratulations on your success
cards.Notes: sofol = successful; sofol hoa = to succeed.
X-er kotha bhabchhi = I'm thinking about X.

cards.English: Could I take tomorrow off? (to your boss)
cards.Romanization: ami ki kal ekdin chhuti nite pari?
cards.Bengali: আমি কি কাল একদিন ছুটি নিতে পারি?
cards.Notes: Polite request to a boss. Many would say 'leave' instead of chhuti.
